column2:
Referral arrives
A new start-of-care referral enters. It is potential work — not capacity used yet.
column4: Referrals sit unassigned; no fast read of whether we even have room to say yes.

column2:
Capacity read  (the hinge)
Do we have open room — right discipline, right area, this week — to take it? Specifically the assessing capacity for the SOC.
column4: Capacity is read from memory or a stale sheet; we turn down work we could staff, or say yes to work we can’t.

column2:
Assign & schedule
Pick the clinician, day and route. Front-load the week, honor ordered frequency, keep continuity where it matters.
column4: Assignments chase whoever’s free, not best fit; routes zig-zag; the week back-loads and Friday overflows.

column2:
Confirm & coordinate
Day-before confirmations, reminders, cover call-outs, rebook changes — so the plan survives contact with the day.
column4: Confirmations are manual and skipped; a Monday call-out goes uncovered; misses aren’t rebooked.

column2:
Deliver the visit
The clinician completes the visit and syncs it. This is the only event that becomes revenue. Completed vs. in-progress vs. missed.
column4: We can’t tell earned from scheduled until docs sync late; missed visits (past, never worked) hide as “scheduled.”

column2:
Outcome & revenue
Delivered visits roll up to 30-day period revenue and compliance; discharges reopen capacity for the next referral.
column4: LUPA risk (too few visits in a period) isn’t seen until too late; reopened capacity isn’t fed back to intake.
